conventions.convention: Use a positive Borel, Q⁺ equal to the nonnegative integral simple-root cone, μ ≤ λ iff λ−μ ∈ Q⁺, and the dot action w·λ = w(λ+ρ)−ρ. A truncation is a lower set of composition labels inside one finite integral-reflection linkage class, not a bound on all module weights.
Projectivity and projective covers are relative to the stated abelian category. An indecomposable object is nonzero; zero has the empty indecomposable decomposition.
A Verma flag is a finite increasing filtration by subobjects with Verma quotients; splitting is not required. Zero has the empty flag and zero multiplicities.

Single-wall data use integral dot-antidominant λ and μ, λ dot-regular, and dot stabilizer Sμ = {1,sα}. Sμ is distinct from the integral-reflection group Wμ, which equals W here. Upper-closure tests use positive roots only.
Translation projects generalized central-character summands. The reverse translating module is the ordinary contragredient dual L(ν)*; restricted Chevalley duality is a different duality.
For dominant integral λ, degree k is the sum of M(w·λ) over ℓ(w)=k. Bruhat arrows point from a cover to the covered element, so differentials lower degree.
Cover maps are compatible inclusions of fixed Verma submodules inside M(λ). Every Bruhat diamond has sign product −1. The augmentation is d₀: M(λ) → L(λ).

Dualizing complexes have bounded coherent cohomology, finite local injective dimension and homothety. Hᵃ(K[b]) = Hᵃ⁺ᵇ(K). Ext_X is global derived Hom, not sheaf Ext. Pure dimension means every irreducible component has the same dimension.

Coherent duality assumes AC and a projective pure d-dimensional CM scheme over a field. The pairing is Yoneda composition followed by the normalized trace; negative Ext and negative sheaf cohomology are zero.

The published smooth regular-immersion Ext comparison multiplies the Koszul determinant identification exactly once by σc = (−1)^(c(c+1)/2); the smooth specialization transports its trace using that identification.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. Every simple L(μ) in category O admits a projective cover inside its linkage class, unique up to isomorphism and indecomposable. Every object of O is a quotient of a finite direct sum of these covers.
Assume AC. For dominant integral λ, Bk(λ) = (Bk^χ₀ ⊗ L(λ))^χλ gives an exact resolution of L(λ) in O, with type {w·λ : ℓ(w)=k}, each weight occurring once.

Assume AC. For a finite map of Noetherian rings, RHom_A(B,−) is right adjoint to restriction of scalars. For a closed immersion of Noetherian schemes, i!G = i⁻¹ RHom_Y(i_*O_X,G) has internal and global derived Hom adjunctions, counit evaluation at 1, and RΓ(Y,i_*K)=RΓ(X,K) for bounded coherent K.

Assume AC. For any μ in a linkage class, including nonintegral or nonreal μ, the specified sufficiently large N gives λ=μ+Nρ maximal in its linkage class and E=L(Nρ) self-dual. M(λ) and E⊗M(λ) are projective in O, and the block projection of E⊗M(λ) maps onto L(μ).
Assume AC. The standard induced complex is exact, giving 0 → B|Φ⁺| → ⋯ → B₁ → B₀ → C → 0 as a resolution of the trivial g-module.
Assume AC, λ dominant integral and k≥0. If the BGG complex is exact in degrees 0,…,k−1, then ker d_k/n⁻ker d_k is finite-dimensional and has dimension dim(Ck+1/n⁻Ck+1)=|Wk+1|.
Assume AC, λ dominant integral and k≥0. Exactness in degrees 0,…,k−1 implies that the induced map Ck+1/n⁻Ck+1 → ker d_k/n⁻ker d_k is injective.
Assume AC. Every projective object of O has a finite Verma flag.
Assume AC. For all weights μ,ν, dim Hom_O(Δ(μ),∇(ν)) is 1 if μ=ν and 0 otherwise, and Ext¹_O(Δ(μ),∇(ν))=0.
Assume AC. On P=P^N_k with ωP=O(−N−1) and Laurent trace, evaluation gives a natural quasi-isomorphism RΓ(P,RHom_P(K,ωP[N])) → RHom_k(RΓ(P,K),k) for every bounded coherent K.

Assume AC. For regular Noetherian A of finite dimension, invertible L, nonzero B=A/I and any integer s, DB=RHom_A(B,L[s]) is dualizing; RHom_B(−,DB) preserves bounded finite cohomology and canonical bidual evaluation is an isomorphism. These assertions localize.

Assume AC. The embedding complex Di=i!(ωP[N]) has counit/Laurent trace inducing Hom_D(X)(K,Di[r]) ≅ Hom_k(H^−r(X,K),k) for bounded coherent K and every integer r. Two embeddings give a unique isomorphism identifying these comparisons and preserving trace.
Assume AC. For projective pure d-dimensional CM X over a field, DX ≅ ωX[d], with ωX=H^−d(DX) coherent, CM and supported on X. For an embedding into P^N, i_*ωX = sheaf Ext_P^(N−d)(i_*O_X,ωP).
Assume AC. For all weights λ,μ, (P(λ):Δ(μ)) = [Δ(μ):L(λ)] = [M(μ):L(λ)].
Assume AC and a single-wall datum. For every w∈W, translation to the wall sends Δ(w·λ) to Δ(w·μ); translation from the wall of Δ(w·μ) has exactly the two Verma factors Δ(w·λ) and Δ(ws·λ), each once.
Assume AC. For dominant integral λ, the augmented signed BGG complex 0 → C|Φ⁺|(λ) → ⋯ → C₀(λ) → L(λ) → 0 is exact.

Assume AC. For projective pure d-dimensional CM X/k, every coherent F and every integer i have a natural perfect trace/composition pairing Ext_X^(d−i)(F,ωX) × H^i(X,F) → k. The bounded coherent complex comparison and coherent biduality also hold without perfectness on X.

concerns.concern: Fact F2 says that morphisms correspond to endomorphisms of the simple quotient and therefore 'form a one-dimensional space.' Simplicity alone only gives a division endomorphism ring. The missing justification here is that L(λ) is generated by its one-dimensional highest-weight space, so every endomorphism is scalar. The assertion is correct, but this short argument is implicit in the base case used by the proof.

Step 2.1 uses 'Restrictions of an injective module sheaf to an open subset remain injective, since extension by zero is exact and left adjoint to restriction.' The cited thm-extension-by-zero-adjunction-exactness states this adjunction and exactness only for sheaves of abelian groups. The proof needs the analogous O-module statement. It follows by equipping extension by zero with the natural O-action and checking exactness stalkwise, but that extension of the cited interface is unstated.
